index_title: Actual finite fibres, invariant classes and the canonical real hull
scope: Preparation for OTHER Lean projects. Five full real_hull files give eighteen numbered results; the selected actual-fibre CCO lemma is the nineteenth export. RAW word-exact calculus, exact CRT, arbitrary imaginary CCO and SAP are not prerequisites. Other results in cco_finite_fibres.tex and real_hull/06–07 are not covered.
scope_explanation: statement and proof. Fibre-closed (source exact for Z) is separate from RAW word exactness. Canonical hull, actual orbit and global class have distinct contracts.

assumptions.name: Elementary original real source
assumptions.statement: One inhabited transitive ultrahomogeneous complete finite named symmetric binary source, actual represented products, and separate logical equality. No CCO, SAP or word-exactness follows from this assumption alone.

assumptions.name: Original age amalgamation
assumptions.statement: The actual age has AP. Wherever complete-diagram triangle fullness is needed it is supplied by the separate named I01 contract, not by SAP.

assumptions.name: Original semantic homomorphic CCO
assumptions.statement: Finite partial diversity diagrams whose specified simple cycles map to the original source have a homomorphism. Used directly for actual fibre/class inheritance, not for arbitrary imaginaries.

assumptions.name: Elementary finite combinatorics
assumptions.statement: Classical finite pigeonhole, finite selection and finite cardinal reasoning. A sufficient finite triangle Ramsey bound is proved internally; no infinite Ramsey theorem is imported.

imports.name: Original triangle fullness
imports.statement: A finite complete original diagram whose induced diagrams on at most three vertices belong to the age belongs to the age. Available from hereditary age AP plus original semantic CCO; source proof is supplied. Consumers may take this exact law explicitly.

imports.name: Full original Hasse index theorem
imports.statement: In an actual homogeneous transitive finite symmetric binary CCO source, all full invariant-equivalence covers of finite relative index have index two. The source may be finite. Instantiate only after inherited fibre/class hypotheses are proved; no exactness of endpoints.

definitions.name: Original elementary source
definitions.statement: Inhabited transitive ultrahomogeneous complete finite symmetric binary source. Original atom names are actual pair orbitals, with logical equality separate.

definitions.name: RAW squares and guarded H
definitions.statement: All products are equality-inclusive represented composition. A_p=(p;p) minus logical equality; H(a,b)=(a;b) intersect diversity, so H(a,a)=A_a. H is not an associative replacement algebra.

definitions.name: Global invariant supports and generated closure
definitions.statement: R is a diversity-name set with R^+={Id} union R composition-closed. It represents any original invariant equivalence, not necessarily word-exact. <S> is its least generated support.

definitions.name: Support orbits and fixedness
definitions.statement: O_R(u)=(R^+;u) intersect diversity; these support-calculus classes partition the palette. R-fixed p means R^+;p={p}, forcing p outside R. These are not Aut-orbits on literal colour names.

definitions.name: Actual realised new-point fibre
definitions.statement: For finite complete real A and realised q(x/A) with x outside A, Z is its actual realization set, one stabilizer orbit; nonempty A gives diversity spokes p_i. The formula T=intersect A_pi is proved, not assumed.

definitions.name: Fibre-closed support (source exact for Z)
definitions.statement: A global invariant equivalence support R whose whole classes meeting actual Z lie in Z. The source also records R subset its palette T. This is NOT a word-exactness assumption.

definitions.name: Canonical spoke-fixer
definitions.statement: For a nonempty actual spoke-name set P, R_P={d:p;d={p} for every p in P}. T_P=intersect A_p is the palette candidate.

definitions.name: Actual invariant class
definitions.statement: For an arbitrary original invariant equivalence E=R^+, C is one actual class. R can be empty (singleton C) or nonexact.

definitions.name: Full internal invariant interval
definitions.statement: InvEq(C) means invariance under FULL Aut(C), compared with original [Id,E]. No onto restriction homomorphism or lattice distributivity is assumed.

definitions.name: Looped colours and fixed-family pseudocomplement
definitions.statement: L={r:r in A_r}. For nonempty R-fixed P set S=intersect A_p and W_R(P)={a:A_a intersect S subset R}; all are diversity support sets.

definitions.name: Carrier insertion data
definitions.statement: A realised finite star with nonempty P and additional spoke b; S=intersect A_p, C=S intersect A_b. Generated supports use the full invariant support closure.

definitions.name: Connectivity and even connectivity
definitions.statement: Gamma(p)=<{p}>, B(p)=<A_p>. B(p)^+ has a positive even-word presentation; Gamma(p)^+ need not be RAW word-exact.

definitions.name: Real algebraicity and canonical class
definitions.statement: Real acl over finite A means finite orbit under Aut(M/A). For x outside A use J=intersect Gamma(col(x,a)) and the intersection of the corresponding anchored classes. Empty A uses universal support; parameter x in A is a separate equality case.

definitions.name: Finite triangle Ramsey number
definitions.statement: For k>=1, R_k(3) is the least sufficient size. Existence is proved by f(0)=1, f(t+1)=k f(t)+1 and k+1 pivots plus one final vertex; no infinite Ramsey input.

claims.name: Elementary finite triangle Ramsey
claims.statement: The recursive pivot bound f_k(k+1) guarantees a monochromatic triangle; two of k+1 pivot colours coincide. Thus R_k(3) exists, including k=1.

claims.name: Original RAW support algebra
claims.statement: Associativity, original commutation, serial nonempty products, equality criterion and Peirce imply invariant support closure and support-orbit calculus.

claims.name: Actual fibre palette and triangle fullness
claims.statement: Over the same complete actual anchor, two-new-point and arbitrary complete extensions show the actual fibre palette is T=intersect A_pi and its induced age is triangle-defined.

claims.name: Relative separator
claims.statement: For a global support R and finite P with intersection A_p subset R, different R-support orbits u,v are separated by some row H(p,u),H(p,v). AP and triangle fullness force the two apexes distinct via different old colours.

claims.name: Rectangle criterion and folding
claims.statement: For distinct u,v, H(p,u) meets H(p,v) iff A_p meets H(u,v). If u~_R v and t in H(u,v) outside R, folding supplies t_prime in A_u outside R in the same support orbit as t; u=v is immediate.

claims.name: Mixed orbit collapse
claims.statement: For R-fixed p and a!=p with A_a intersect A_p subset R, a;p is exactly one nonempty diversity support orbit.

claims.name: Self-side collapse
claims.statement: For an R-fixed p, if c in A_p and A_c intersect A_p subset R, then p;c={p} and A_c subset R, with c=p excluded by fixedness.

claims.name: Minimal-blocker square avoidance
claims.statement: For inclusion-minimal finite B with intersection A_b subset R, p in B R-fixed, and S_i=(intersection of the other rows) minus R, every A_a with a in A_p avoids S_i. Keep equality, d=p and d in R branches explicit.

claims.name: Fibre stabilizer orbit and homogeneity
claims.statement: The actual fibre is transitive and homogeneous by adjoining the complete actual anchor to finite partial maps; the empty map uses identity. No globalisation is used. The realised type is a finite conjunction of spoke formulas and inequalities, so its orbit is definable; usual real algebraicity over finite A is equivalent to the finite-orbit condition.

claims.name: Actual fibre CCO
claims.statement: Adjoin one shared complete anchor, map mixed-cycle fibre path segments independently by stabilizer seriality, apply original homomorphic CCO and align the anchor.

claims.name: Spoke fixedness from whole-class containment
claims.statement: A fibre-closed global support fixes every actual spoke. Equality-output witnesses would put an anchor in the new-point fibre and are excluded.

claims.name: Original spoke-square localisation
claims.statement: For nonempty R-fixed P, c in T and A_c intersect T subset R imply A_c subset R and p;c={p} for every p. Prove by minimal blockers before globalisation.

claims.name: Canonical spoke-fixer equivalence and maximality
claims.statement: R_P is globally composition-closed by associativity/nonempty products and is largest among supports fixing all spokes. No finiteness or CCO argument is used.

claims.name: Spoke-fixer classes stay in the fibre
claims.statement: Every R_P-class meeting Z stays in Z; transitivity and the actual palette formula give R_P subset T.

claims.name: Finite internal Hasse and sizes before globalisation
claims.statement: For finite actual Z, inherited homogeneity/CCO give all full internal covers index two and |Z|=2^m with m<=|D|, by a saturated chain and actual atom count.

claims.name: One-cover square transfer forces equality
claims.statement: For a FINITE actual fibre Z over a NONEMPTY complete anchor, if R_P<T select one full internal cover above its restriction. Three new q-points transfer internal squares to A_c intersect T subset R_P; localisation contradicts the cover layer. Thus R_P=T and Z is its whole class.

claims.name: Finite-fibre global equivalence including boundaries
claims.statement: Nonempty anchor uses C16. Empty anchor gives Z=M, finite only when M is finite, with universal support. A singleton fibre gives true equality, not an artificial diversity atom.

claims.name: Globalise all internal chains after existence
claims.statement: After Z is one global E_T-class, apply the independent generic interval isomorphism. All internal chains lift with index preservation and uniqueness within [Id,E_T].

claims.name: Spoke-set criterion and uniform conjugacy
claims.statement: For every realised type with the same nonempty P, Z is one R_P-class iff T=R_P. Finiteness additionally requires finite class size; one finite instance forces common two-power size and conjugacy of all such fibres, not transport of anchors.

claims.name: Elementary class palette/homogeneity
claims.statement: For any original E-class C, each old E-colour occurs in C and is an orbital of full Aut(C). The class is transitive and homogeneous. No CCO/SAP/globalisation is used.

claims.name: Generic full internal interval isomorphism
claims.statement: Literal old-atom unions extend internal invariant equivalences uniquely within [Id,E]. Transitivity is checked by moving an entire E-class into C. No globalisation or extension of every Aut(C) is assumed.

claims.name: Class triangle fullness and CCO
claims.statement: Use original triangle fullness for complete class diagrams; map distinct specified-edge components into C independently after original CCO.

claims.name: Full finite-class interval covers
claims.statement: For finite-class original E, a cover in [Id,E] is a full original cover with finite relative index, so the original Hasse provider gives index two directly. No exactness of E is required.

claims.name: Two-power class size with atom bound
claims.statement: A saturated chain below finite-class E gives size 2^m, and each step adds at least one old diversity atom, so m<=|R|. Full invariant intervals may be M3.

claims.name: Fixed-family outside-R saturation
claims.statement: For nonempty R-fixed P, R subset W and each A_p minus R, hence S minus R, is saturated under support orbits, with equality outputs treated before removal.

claims.name: Pseudocomplement square closure
claims.statement: For a in W and x in A_a, an outside-R witness from A_x contradicts separator/folding. Handle intermediate equality and d=a cases separately.

claims.name: Pseudocomplement mixed closure
claims.statement: For distinct a,b in W and c in a;b, use rectangle/separator/folding to rule out A_c intersect S minus R. Together with square closure this makes W a global support.

claims.name: Carrier fibre and finite loop-free bound
claims.statement: An actual star with P plus b has palette exactly C=S intersect A_b. If C has no looped colour, finite triangle Ramsey makes its actual nonempty fibre finite, including C empty.

claims.name: Carrier insertion
claims.statement: Globalise the finite carrier fibre, use spoke fixedness and W_C(P); its containment of b and generated A_b contradicts a looped r in S intersect <A_b> outside C.

claims.name: Looped diagonal Helly
claims.statement: Process finitely many rows using carrier insertion with the extra current looped colour as a row; A_r containment preserves remaining generated-support constraints. Empty input is tautological.

claims.name: Even connectivity and the odd-sheet obstruction
claims.statement: B(p) is even-walk connectivity with index at most two in Gamma(p). A looped colour cannot cross the odd sheet. Positive even profiles stabilize; Gamma need not be RAW exact.

claims.name: Finite fibre excludes every looped colour
claims.statement: A looped colour in T permits arbitrarily large cliques of new q-points over the actual anchor by triangle fullness, contradicting finiteness. No Ramsey, SAP or globalisation is used.

claims.name: Every canonical J-class is uniformly small
claims.statement: No E_J-class contains R_k(3) DISTINCT points: such a finite subset yields a looped colour by Ramsey, even connectivity and looped Helly, contradicting C32. Thus every E_J-class is FINITE with cardinality <R_k(3); do not use Nat.card of an unproved-finite class as a substitute.

claims.name: Canonical hull is the actual J-class
claims.statement: The anchored Gamma-class intersection equals [x]_J and contains the anchor-stabilizer orbit. By C33 it is finite; it need not equal the one-point fibre.

claims.name: Empty-base and parameter conventions
claims.statement: For empty base, Z=M by transitivity; finite M is loop-free by clique extension and satisfies the finite Ramsey bound. For x in A use equality directly, without applying diversity Gamma to Id.

claims.name: Two-power canonical hull bound
claims.statement: Only after canonical finiteness, apply the finite-class bound to E_J: size is 2^m<=2^|J|<=2^|D|, including finite M with empty anchor.

tasks.name: Finite Ramsey and elementary actual fibre/class geometry
tasks.acceptance: Prove finite Ramsey, source support algebra, actual fibre inheritance and generic class interval independently of globalisation.

tasks.name: Relative separator and localisation
tasks.acceptance: Prove AP/triangle separator, rectangle/folding, collapse and square localisation, retaining all logical-identity branches.

tasks.name: Direct finite-fibre globalisation
tasks.acceptance: Construct R_P before finiteness, use one internal cover and three-new-point transfer, then apply the independent class interval for chain lifting and uniformity.

tasks.name: Finite original class bounds
tasks.acceptance: Apply full original Hasse in finite-class intervals and count old atom additions; no exact-lattice distributivity.

tasks.name: Pseudocomplement and looped insertion
tasks.acceptance: Prove W closure, finite carrier insertion and looped diagonal Helly without RAW exact Helly or infinite Ramsey.

tasks.name: Canonical real hull
tasks.acceptance: Separate even connectivity, finite-fibre loop exclusion, Ramsey canonical finiteness and subsequent two-power bound; retain boundary and orbit/hull distinctions.

controls.check: Infinite-block F2² packet algebra: full finite packet interval M3, nonexact connectivity and packet equivalences, with all finite interval covers index two.
Nested two-bit packet model: 28 realised anchored types, spoke-fixer/palette equality, uniform sizes, and strict distinction between the two-point fibre and four-point canonical hull.
Relative separator, rectangle/folding, minimal blockers, pseudocomplement closure and looped Helly on represented packet/ultrametric palettes.
Tiny gain-labelled diagrams for the two source examples: cycle tests match simultaneous homomorphic completion; finite snapshots are not claimed globally CCO.
Finite triangle Ramsey on all 32768 two-colourings of K6, plus recurrence bounds and the unrestricted-lift uniqueness counterexample.

article_feedback.finding: Uniqueness is among original lifts below E_T, equivalently fibre-closed for Z. Unrestricted global uniqueness is false because E_T and Top both restrict to internal Top_Z.
article_feedback.proposed_article_change: Write unique lift in [Id,E_T]; theorem conclusions stay unchanged.
article_feedback.caller_effect: No source theorem hypothesis or conclusion changes; clarifies the contracts and avoids false imports.

article_feedback.finding: Exact for Z means whole-class containment, not RAW word-exactness. Internal lifted equivalences may be nonexact word relations.

article_feedback.caller_effect: No source theorem hypothesis or conclusion changes; clarifies the contracts and avoids false imports.

review.method: Two independent read-only model reviews of finite-fibre/globalisation and invariant-class/loop/canonical branches, plus parent synthesis and finite controls. Not human or Lean certification.
review.remaining: Other projects must implement the source, finite graph, support, fibre and interval contracts in Lean. The uniqueness proof phrase needs its intended interval scope; no theorem conclusion changes.
